goals: PRIMARY (infeasible as posed): quantify hillslope-to-stream travel times including lateral flow convergence and inter-hillslope groundwater exchange

PRECURSOR (partial): characterize how VERTICAL water partitioning (recharge, sub-surface drainage, water-table depth) varies with topographic/hillslope position, as boundary-condition input for a future lateral transport model
key_processes: lateral subsurface flow convergence along flowpaths (NOT representable)
groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions (NOT representable)
vertical recharge and sub-surface drainage per column (representable)
equilibrium water-table depth per column (representable via warm start)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column can supply per-position vertical fluxes, but the question's core mechanisms are lateral and cannot be represented; ELM alone cannot compute travel times.
model_choice.coupling_note: Travel times and inter-hillslope exchange require lateral flow + routing/particle tracking that ELM lacks. A true answer needs ELM coupled to a lateral groundwater model (PFLOTRAN/ParFlow) PLUS a flowpath connectivity and travel-time tracker. Listed in requires_capabilities.

answerable: vertical recharge and sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) per stratified hillslope position
per-column equilibrium water-table depth (via Fan-2013 WTD warm start) as a static field, NOT its lateral evolution
how topography/elevation modulates VERTICAL water balance via NLDAS forcing variation

not_answerable.why: single-column ELM has no lateral transport, no routing, and no particle/flowpath tracking; travel time is a connected-flowpath quantity that no component computes

not_answerable.aspect: lateral flow convergence along topographic flowpaths
not_answerable.why: columns are independent 1-D points with no column-to-column exchange; convergence cannot occur
not_answerable.needs: lateral subsurface flow model / ELM->PFLOTRAN(ParFlow) coupling

not_answerable.aspect: groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
not_answerable.why: no lateral/regional groundwater flow; each column has an isolated 1-D aquifer

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by hillslope position (topographic) x dominant soil, as a HILLSLOPE-SEQUENCE precursor sampling (NOT a travel-time design)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 topographic positions x ~2 dominant soil classes = 8 baseline strata, plus light replication (~4) in valley/riparian and lower-midslope where vertical drainage->lateral-exchange coupling would be strongest, to bracket variability. This spans the hillslope gradient enough to build the vertical-flux boundary field a future lateral model needs; a denser grid buys nothing while the lateral mechanism remains unrepresentable.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in valley bottoms / riparian corridors and lower midslopes where recharge convergence and groundwater-soil-moisture exchange would dominate; sample ridge/upland to bracket the recharge-source end of the (conceptual) flowpath. Downstream expander samples DEM position and SSURGO to realize points.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2x light replication in valley/riparian and lower-midslope strata to capture soil-driven spread where exchange fluxes matter most

sampling_plan.reason: brackets the upslope recharge-generation end of the conceptual flowpath; supplies vertical drainage input for a future lateral model
characterizes vertical partitioning where downslope through-flow would originate; no lateral flow captured, position only
replicated across soil classes because this is where vertical drainage feeding lateral convergence is strongest; brackets soil-driven flux spread
replicated where groundwater exchange and shallow water tables dominate; provides the discharge-end boundary flux, though lateral exchange itself is unrepresentable

validation_design.comparison: none possible in-domain; could only be analog process check against literature hillslope recharge gradients (clearly analog, not co-located)
validation_design.metric: qualitative consistency with expected downslope recharge/WTD gradient

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 baseline forcing, native SSURGO soil, Fan-2013 WTD warm start, multi-year spin-up (recharge/WTD are targets)

requires_capabilities.why: travel time is a connected-flowpath transport quantity
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire primary question (hillslope-to-stream travel times)

requires_capabilities.capability: lateral subsurface flow model / ELM->PFLOTRAN or ParFlow coupling
requires_capabilities.why: convergence and downslope through-flow require column-to-column lateral transport
single-column aquifers are isolated with no lateral exchange
requires_capabilities.blocks: groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff/subsurface routing + aggregation to stream network
requires_capabilities.why: 'to-stream' implies a routed drainage network absent from single-column ELM
recharge and water table are slow states that are init artifacts without spin-up
requires_capabilities.blocks: meaningful per-position vertical recharge/WTD (the precursor product)

requires_capabilities.capability: in-domain observation ingest (streamflow gages, wells, isotope/tracer travel-time data)
requires_capabilities.why: no observations provided; travel-time validation typically needs tracer/hydrograph data

assumptions: Naches is within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 12 km elevation-modulated forcing is available across the 1625 m relief.
SSURGO soils and a DEM are available for the downstream expander to realize hillslope-position and soil strata.
The precursor vertical-flux product is only useful if a lateral coupling capability is later built; delivered alone it does NOT answer the user's question.
Sub-12 km terrain is unresolved, so within-hillslope forcing gradients finer than the NLDAS cell are not captured.
open_questions: Does the user accept a vertical-flux boundary-condition precursor, or is only an actual travel-time answer acceptable (in which case the request is blocked pending lateral coupling)?
Are any tracer, well, or gage observations obtainable for the Naches to eventually constrain lateral transport?
Is a ParFlow-CONUS2 / PFLOTRAN coupling on the development roadmap, and on what timeline?
What spatial/temporal resolution of travel time is required (event vs mean transit time)?
